Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 110, verse 1–3:

Madaniyya; it has ninety-seven letters, sixteen words, and three verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Hayyari informed me, from Marra, who said: Al-Imam Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili al-Jurjani and Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz al-Asbahani informed us, both saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abi Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Yarbu'i narrated to us, saying: Salam narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Fath, it is as if he witnessed with Muhammad the conquest of Makkah" [288] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/466.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ over those who opposed you and were hostile to you. Yaman said: it refers to the conquest of cities and palaces. The majority of exegetes said: the conquest of Makkah.

Its story, as related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Bashshar and the scholars of narratives, is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concluded the treaty with Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyya, among the conditions was that whoever wished to enter into the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could enter it, and whoever wished to enter into the pact and covenant of Quraysh could enter it. So Banu Bakr entered into the pact of Quraysh, and Khuza'a entered into the pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Between them there had been an old enmity. The cause that stirred up what was between Bakr and Khuza'a was that a man from Hadramawt called Malik ibn 'Abbad went out as a merchant, and when he passed through the land of Khuza'a, they attacked him and killed him. Then, before Islam, Khuza'a attacked the clan of al-Aswad ibn Razin al-Dili, who were among the nobles of Bakr, and killed him at 'Arafa near the boundary markers of the sanctuary. While Bakr and Khuza'a were in this state of hostility, Islam held them back and people became occupied with it. But when the treaty of al-Hudaybiyya occurred and that truce was established, Banu al-Dil of Banu Bakr seized the opportunity against Khuza'a and wished to strike at them in revenge for those men who had killed the sons of al-Aswad ibn Razin. Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Dili went out with Banu al-Dil, and he was their leader that day, until they ambushed Khuza'a while they were at al-Watir, a water source for them below Makkah. They struck down a man from them, and they disputed and fought. Quraysh supplied Banu Bakr with weapons, and some of Quraysh fought with them by night, concealing themselves, until they crossed Khuza'a toward the sanctuary. Among those from Quraysh who aided Banu Bakr against Khuza'a for two nights, personally participating, were Safwan ibn Umayya, 'Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr, along with their slaves. They said: When they reached the sanctuary, Banu Bakr said: "O Nawfal, we have entered the sanctuary; your god, your god!" He said a great word: "There is no god today [O Banu Bakr]. Take your revenge in it. By my life, you steal in the sanctuary; will you not take your revenge in it?" [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/324.]].

When Khuza'a entered Makkah, they took refuge in the house of Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i and the house of a client of theirs called Rafi'. When Quraysh backed Banu Bakr against Khuza'a, inflicted on them what they inflicted, and broke what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the covenant, regarding what they made lawful against Khuza'a, while they were under the covenant, 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i went out and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was among what stirred the conquest of Makkah. He stood before him while he was sitting in the mosque among the people and said to them: "I have pledged to Muhammad," and he recited the verses as they are recorded in Surat al-Tawba, up to his saying:

"They attacked us at al-Watir while we were sleeping, so they killed us while bowing and prostrating." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/325.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have been helped, O 'Amr ibn Salim." Then a cloud appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the sky, and he said: "Indeed this cloud is announcing the victory of the Banu Ka'b." [And the Messenger of Allah ordered the people to prepare, and concealed from them his destination.]

Hassan said, reaching him of the conversion of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, whose name was Hind:

"Has Hind's question stirred your longing, as do separation and its departure..." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/340; al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 4/318.]]

[The poem.]

Ibn Ishaq said: all of the Muslims who witnessed the conquest of Makkah numbered ten thousand: four hundred from Banu Ghifar, four hundred from Aslam, a thousand from Muzayna, seven hundred from Banu Sulaym, a thousand four hundred men from Juhayna, and the rest from Quraysh, the Ansar and their allies, and groups of the Arabs from Tamim, Qays and Asad.

They said: the conquest of Makkah was ten nights before the end of Ramadan in the year eight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah after its conquest for fifteen nights, shortening the prayer. Then he went out toward Hawazin and Thaqif, who had camped at Hunayn.

﴿And you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾, groups and successive companies [[al-Arsal: one group after another; its singular is rasl.]] — an entire tribe at once, and whole peoples without fighting.

Al-Hasan said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, the Arabs said to one another: "Since Muhammad has triumphed over the people of the sanctuary, and God had protected them from the companions of the elephant, you have no power against him." So they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes.

'Ikrima and Muqatil said: by "the people" he meant the people of Yemen.

Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayra said:

When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar, the help of Allah and the victory have come" [[Mawarid al-Zam'an: 572, where it reads: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar.]]. And the people of Yemen came: people whose hearts are tender and soft, whose obedience is faith, "Faith is Yemeni, understanding is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musaffar narrated to us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: a neighbor of Jabir narrated to me, saying: Jabir came in the morning to greet me, and he began asking me about the condition of the people. I began informing him of something like what I had seen of their disagreement and division, and I was telling him while he wept. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and they will leave the religion of Allah in multitudes" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/343.]].

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ That is, then you will soon join Him, and you will taste death as those messengers before you tasted it. At completion, decline is awaited, as it has been said:

"When a matter is completed in its perfection, expect its decline; when it is said 'it is complete'..." [[In the source: badā (appeared) instead of "tamma" wording variation.]] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/467.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to admit the people of Badr, and he would admit me with them. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said: "Do you admit this youth with us, when among our sons there is one like him?" 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." Ibn 'Abbas said: So one day he admitted them, and admitted me with them, and he asked them about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ to the end of the verse. I do not think he asked them except on my account. Some of them said: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ), when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness and repent to Him. Then he asked me, and I said: "It is not so; rather, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of the approach of his term, and his own self was announced to him, and that is the sign of his death." 'Umar said: "I know of it only what you know," then he said:

"How do you blame me for it, after what you see..." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/338, with slight variation.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri informed us, saying: Ibn Fadl narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My self has been announced to me," meaning that he would be taken in that year [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/217.]].

Muqatil and Qatada said: the Prophet (ﷺ) lived two years after the revelation of this surah.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying:

Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would often say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; forgive me, indeed You are the Accepting of repentance" [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/434.]].

Abd Allah informed us, saying: Makki informed me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would often say before he died: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are these words that I see you have newly made, saying them?" He said: "I have made it a sign in my community: when I see it, I say it: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾" to the end of the surah.

With the same chain, from Ibn Hashim, who said: Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Muslim, that is Ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her and with her father, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed to its end, I never saw the Prophet (ﷺ) pray a prayer except that he said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, O Allah, forgive me" [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/230.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm Salama, who said: Toward the end of his life, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not stand, sit, come, or go except that he said: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, you do not stand, sit, come, or go except that you say: Glory be to Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him." He said: "Indeed I have been commanded with it" [[Jami' al-Bayan li al-Tabari: 30/435.]], then he recited ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ until he completed it.

Muqatil said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to his companions, among whom were Abu Bakr, 'Umar and Sa'id ibn Abi al-'As, and they rejoiced and were glad. Al-'Abbas heard it and wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep, O uncle?" He said: "Your self has been announced to you." He said: "Indeed it is as you say" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/232.]]. He lived after it two years, and he was not seen laughing or joyful during them.

This surah is called Surat al-Tawdi' (the Surah of Farewell).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Darda' Abd al-'Aziz ibn Munayb narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Kaysan narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back from the battle of Hunayn, and the surah ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'Ali, and O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad: the help of Allah and the victory have come, and I have seen the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes. Glory be to my Lord, with His praise, and I seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance. And O 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, after me there will be fighting among the believers." 'Ali said: "Do we fight the believers who say 'We have faith'?" He said: "Against those who introduce innovations in the religion when they act by opinion; there is no opinion in religion. Religion is only from the Lord: His command and His prohibition."

'Ali said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if a matter arises concerning which Allah has not made clear a Qur'an and no Sunna from you has been stated?" He said: "Make it a matter of consultation among the worshippers [[In the source: "among the believers."]], and do not decide by private opinion. Even if I were to appoint a successor, no one would be more worthy than you, because of your precedence in Islam, your kinship with the Messenger of Allah, and your marriage tie; and with you is Fatima, leader of the women of the believers. And before that, there was what Abu Talib suffered for me when the Qur'an was revealed. So I am eager that this be preserved for his offspring" [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/180; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/295, with slight variation.]].

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mus'ab al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed, al-'Abbas came to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Go in to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If this matter after him is for us, the Quraysh will not dispute it with us; and if it is for someone else, ask him to commend us." 'Ali said: "I will do so." Then al-'Abbas entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) happily and mentioned that to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah has made Abu Bakr my successor over the religion of Allah, the Exalted, and His revelation. So listen to him, and you will be guided; obey him, and you will be rightly guided" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/550, no. 32586.]].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Then they sat, by Allah, and they were rightly guided."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'Ali, and O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad: the help of Allah and the victory have come, and I have seen the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes. Glory be to my Lord, with His praise, and I seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance. And O 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, after me there will be fighting among the believers." 'Ali said: "Do we fight the believers who say 'We have faith'?" He said: "Against those who introduce innovations in the religion when they act by opinion; there is no opinion in religion. Religion is only from the Lord: His command and His prohibition."

'Ali said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if a matter arises concerning which Allah has not made clear a Qur'an and no Sunna from you has been stated?" He said: "Make it a matter of consultation among the worshippers [[In the source: "among the believers."]], and do not decide by private opinion. Even if I were to appoint a successor, no one would be more worthy than you, because of your precedence in Islam, your kinship with the Messenger of Allah, and your marriage tie; and with you is Fatima, leader of the women of the believers. And before that, there was what Abu Talib suffered for me when the Qur'an was revealed. So I am eager that this be preserved for his offspring" [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/180; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/295, with slight variation.]].

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mus'ab al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed, al-'Abbas came to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Go in to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If this matter after him is for us, the Quraysh will not dispute it with us; and if it is for someone else, ask him to commend us." 'Ali said: "I will do so." Then al-'Abbas entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) happily and mentioned that to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah has made Abu Bakr my successor over the religion of Allah, the Exalted, and His revelation. So listen to him, and you will be guided; obey him, and you will be rightly guided" [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/550, no. 32586.]].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Then they sat, by Allah, and they were rightly guided."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 110, verse 1–3:

Madaniyya; it has ninety-seven letters, sixteen words, and three verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Hayyari informed me, from Marra, who said: Al-Imam Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili al-Jurjani and Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz al-Asbahani informed us, both saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abi Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Yarbu'i narrated to us, saying: Salam narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Fath, it is as if he witnessed with Muhammad the conquest of Makkah" [288] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/466.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ over those who opposed you and were hostile to you. Yaman said: it refers to the conquest of cities and palaces. The majority of exegetes said: the conquest of Makkah.

Its story, as related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Bashshar and the scholars of narratives, is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concluded the treaty with Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyya, among the conditions was that whoever wished to enter into the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could enter it, and whoever wished to enter into the pact and covenant of Quraysh could enter it. So Banu Bakr entered into the pact of Quraysh, and Khuza'a entered into the pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Between them there had been an old enmity. The cause that stirred up what was between Bakr and Khuza'a was that a man from Hadramawt called Malik ibn 'Abbad went out as a merchant, and when he passed through the land of Khuza'a, they attacked him and killed him. Then, before Islam, Khuza'a attacked the clan of al-Aswad ibn Razin al-Dili, who were among the nobles of Bakr, and killed him at 'Arafa near the boundary markers of the sanctuary. While Bakr and Khuza'a were in this state of hostility, Islam held them back and people became occupied with it. But when the treaty of al-Hudaybiyya occurred and that truce was established, Banu al-Dil of Banu Bakr seized the opportunity against Khuza'a and wished to strike at them in revenge for those men who had killed the sons of al-Aswad ibn Razin. Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Dili went out with Banu al-Dil, and he was their leader that day, until they ambushed Khuza'a while they were at al-Watir, a water source for them below Makkah. They struck down a man from them, and they disputed and fought. Quraysh supplied Banu Bakr with weapons, and some of Quraysh fought with them by night, concealing themselves, until they crossed Khuza'a toward the sanctuary. Among those from Quraysh who aided Banu Bakr against Khuza'a for two nights, personally participating, were Safwan ibn Umayya, 'Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr, along with their slaves. They said: When they reached the sanctuary, Banu Bakr said: "O Nawfal, we have entered the sanctuary; your god, your god!" He said a great word: "There is no god today [O Banu Bakr]. Take your revenge in it. By my life, you steal in the sanctuary; will you not take your revenge in it?" [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/324.]].

When Khuza'a entered Makkah, they took refuge in the house of Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i and the house of a client of theirs called Rafi'. When Quraysh backed Banu Bakr against Khuza'a, inflicted on them what they inflicted, and broke what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the covenant, regarding what they made lawful against Khuza'a, while they were under the covenant, 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i went out and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was among what stirred the conquest of Makkah. He stood before him while he was sitting in the mosque among the people and said to them: "I have pledged to Muhammad," and he recited the verses as they are recorded in Surat al-Tawba, up to his saying:

"They attacked us at al-Watir while we were sleeping, so they killed us while bowing and prostrating." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/325.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have been helped, O 'Amr ibn Salim." Then a cloud appeared to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the sky, and he said: "Indeed this cloud is announcing the victory of the Banu Ka'b." [And the Messenger of Allah ordered the people to prepare, and concealed from them his destination.]

Hassan said, reaching him of the conversion of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, whose name was Hind:

"Has Hind's question stirred your longing, as do separation and its departure..." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/340; al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 4/318.]]

[The poem.]

Ibn Ishaq said: all of the Muslims who witnessed the conquest of Makkah numbered ten thousand: four hundred from Banu Ghifar, four hundred from Aslam, a thousand from Muzayna, seven hundred from Banu Sulaym, a thousand four hundred men from Juhayna, and the rest from Quraysh, the Ansar and their allies, and groups of the Arabs from Tamim, Qays and Asad.

They said: the conquest of Makkah was ten nights before the end of Ramadan in the year eight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah after its conquest for fifteen nights, shortening the prayer. Then he went out toward Hawazin and Thaqif, who had camped at Hunayn.

﴿And you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾, groups and successive companies [[al-Arsal: one group after another; its singular is rasl.]] — an entire tribe at once, and whole peoples without fighting.

Al-Hasan said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, the Arabs said to one another: "Since Muhammad has triumphed over the people of the sanctuary, and God had protected them from the companions of the elephant, you have no power against him." So they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes.

'Ikrima and Muqatil said: by "the people" he meant the people of Yemen.

Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayra said:

When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar, the help of Allah and the victory have come" [[Mawarid al-Zam'an: 572, where it reads: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar.]]. And the people of Yemen came: people whose hearts are tender and soft, whose obedience is faith, "Faith is Yemeni, understanding is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musaffar narrated to us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: a neighbor of Jabir narrated to me, saying: Jabir came in the morning to greet me, and he began asking me about the condition of the people. I began informing him of something like what I had seen of their disagreement and division, and I was telling him while he wept. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and they will leave the religion of Allah in multitudes" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/343.]].

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ That is, then you will soon join Him, and you will taste death as those messengers before you tasted it. At completion, decline is awaited, as it has been said:

"When a matter is completed in its perfection, expect its decline; when it is said 'it is complete'..." [[In the source: badā (appeared) instead of "tamma" wording variation.]] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/467.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to admit the people of Badr, and he would admit me with them. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said: "Do you admit this youth with us, when among our sons there is one like him?" 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." Ibn 'Abbas said: So one day he admitted them, and admitted me with them, and he asked them about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ to the end of the verse. I do not think he asked them except on my account. Some of them said: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ), when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness and repent to Him. Then he asked me, and I said: "It is not so; rather, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of the approach of his term, and his own self was announced to him, and that is the sign of his death." 'Umar said: "I know of it only what you know," then he said:

"How do you blame me for it, after what you see..." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/338, with slight variation.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri informed us, saying: Ibn Fadl narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My self has been announced to me," meaning that he would be taken in that year [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/217.]].

Muqatil and Qatada said: the Prophet (ﷺ) lived two years after the revelation of this surah.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying:

Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would often say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; forgive me, indeed You are the Accepting of repentance" [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/434.]].

Abd Allah informed us, saying: Makki informed me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would often say before he died: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are these words that I see you have newly made, saying them?" He said: "I have made it a sign in my community: when I see it, I say it: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾" to the end of the surah.

With the same chain, from Ibn Hashim, who said: Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Muslim, that is Ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her and with her father, who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed to its end, I never saw the Prophet (ﷺ) pray a prayer except that he said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, O Allah, forgive me" [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/230.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm Salama, who said: Toward the end of his life, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not stand, sit, come, or go except that he said: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, you do not stand, sit, come, or go except that you say: Glory be to Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him." He said: "Indeed I have been commanded with it" [[Jami' al-Bayan li al-Tabari: 30/435.]], then he recited ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ until he completed it.

Muqatil said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to his companions, among whom were Abu Bakr, 'Umar and Sa'id ibn Abi al-'As, and they rejoiced and were glad. Al-'Abbas heard it and wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep, O uncle?" He said: "Your self has been announced to you." He said: "Indeed it is as you say" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/232.]]. He lived after it two years, and he was not seen laughing or joyful during them.

This surah is called Surat al-Tawdi' (the Surah of Farewell).
